newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Johnnic cautionary after Nethold deal.
newsitem.headline: Johnnic cautionary after Nethold deal.

text.p: Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd advised shareholders to exercise caution in dealings following the suspension of the listings of MIH Holdings Ltd and Omni Media Corp Ltd last Friday.

Following the announcement late Friday of the link-up between MIH's associated Dutch satellite television company Nethold BV and French subscriber television station Canal Plus, MIH and Omni published cautionary announcements.

Johnnic, through Omni, has a 15 percent stake in MIH and an effective ordinary shareholding in Nethold of about 11.6 percent. Omni owns 35 percent of MIH and has an effective ordinary shareholding in Nethold of 14.1 percent.
Omni and MIH's listings were due to be reinstated on Monday.
Johnnic cautioned shareholders in dealings until full details of the MIH transaction had been published.
Canal Plus will buy 100 percent of the capital of Nethold from Richemont SA and MIH, paying with 6.1 million new Canal Plus shares and $45 million in cash.
Following the issue of new shares, Richemont and MIH will respectively own 15 and five percent of the enlarged Canal Plus, a statement from the French firm said.
Prior to the completion of the proposed link-up, Nethold will transfer its operations in Africa, the Middle East and the Eastern Mediterranean to MIH.
The Nethold-Canal PLus link-up was preceded by the earlier suspension on Friday on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange of the listings of Richemont Securities AG as well as MIH and Omni.
The Swiss Stock Exchange also suspended Richemont trading in Zurich, where the company has its primary listing.
